title: Reform Movements in India under the British Rule

notes.content:
**Executive summary:** In the **19th century** Indian reformers worked to remove **narrow-minded social and religious practices**. This **social and cultural revival (renaissance)** began in **Bengal** and spread across India.

**Background:** English education grew — **Hindu College, Calcutta (1817)**, **Elphinstone College, Bombay (1856)** produced an English-educated elite; Western habits caused conflict with traditional society; British critics of the treatment of women made Indians look at their own society.

**Factors behind the renaissance**
• Realisation that some **customs were unjust**.
• **Scientific and rational ideas** from Western education.
• **Pride in India's past**.
• A **middle class** able to demand reform.

notes.subtopic: 2. Raja Ram Mohan Roy and the Brahmo Samaj

fiveW.who: Raja Ram Mohan Roy; Lord William Bentinck
fiveW.what: Brahmo Samaj — first organised Hindu reform movement
fiveW.why: To end sati, child marriage, caste rigidity and exploitation by priests
fiveW.how: Writings, campaigns, schools; persuaded Bentinck to make sati a crime

notes.content:
• Scholar who believed **all religions share the same basic truths**; condemned priests who misled people.
• Fought **polygamy, female infanticide, rigid caste, sati, child marriage**.
• Founded the **Brahmo Samaj (1828)**.

**Reforms of the Brahmo Samaj:** abolition of **sati and child marriage** · **widow remarriage** · rejection of **caste** · **modern education** for all · **equal rights for women** and right to **property**.

• Believed **Western education** spreads progressive ideas — helped found **Hindu College** (now Presidency University) and **Vedanta College**.
• His efforts made **Lord William Bentinck ban sati** — it became a **crime punishable by law**.

fiveW.what: Widow remarriage, girls' education, Sanskrit for all
fiveW.why: Pained by the plight of widows; believed women's emancipation was crucial
fiveW.how: Campaigned despite enemies; opened schools; reformed Sanskrit College

notes.content:
• **Humanist** who championed the poor and underprivileged.
• Took up the cause of **widows** — despite many enemies → **Widow Remarriage Act, 1856**.
• Ended the **Brahmanas' monopoly on Sanskrit** — admitted non-Brahmanas.
• Believed **emancipation of women** was vital.
• Helped **Drinkwater Bethune** set up one of the first **girls' schools** in Calcutta (**1849**); opened more girls' schools.
• Introduced **Western philosophy** at the **Sanskrit College**, Calcutta.

fiveW.who: Swami Vivekananda (Narendra Nath Datta), disciple of Ramakrishna Paramahamsa
fiveW.what: Ramakrishna Mission — religious and social service
fiveW.why: To spread Ramakrishna's teachings and regenerate Indians
fiveW.how: Preached unity of religions and service; opened educational institutions

notes.content:
**Ramakrishna Paramahamsa:** all religions are **different paths to one God**; **service to mankind is service to God**.

**Swami Vivekananda** (Narendra Nath Datta) believed in:
• **Unity of all religions**; tolerance, brotherhood, peace.
• Condemned **caste**, inequality, **ritualism and superstition**.
• Regeneration through **self-discipline** and responsibility to society.
• **Upliftment of women**.

Founded the **Ramakrishna Mission** and educational institutions.

notes.subtopic: 5. Western India — Prarthana Samaj, Phule, Arya Samaj

fiveW.who: M.G. Ranade & R.G. Bhandarkar; Jyotirao Phule; Dayanand Saraswati
fiveW.where: Bombay and Maharashtra; north and west India
fiveW.what: Prarthana Samaj, Satyashodhak Samaj, Arya Samaj
fiveW.why: Against child marriage, caste and oppression of women and lower castes
fiveW.how: Schools, campaigns, opening Vedic study and education to all

notes.content:
**Prarthana Samaj** (Bombay, **1860s**) — **Mahadev Govind Ranade, R.G. Bhandarkar**: against **child marriage**; for education, **widow remarriage**, women's education, **Hindu-Muslim unity**.
• **Ramabai Ranade** — early women's rights activist, married at 11; educated herself with her husband's encouragement.

**Jyotirao Govindrao Phule** — worked for **women and untouchable castes**; founded the **Satyashodhak Samaj (1873)** for the oppressed.

**Arya Samaj (1875)** — **Dayanand Saraswati**: against **child marriage, idol worship, caste**; opened **Vedic study to all castes**.
• **DAV (Dayanand Anglo-Vedic) schools** — blend of Indian learning and Western science.

notes.subtopic: 6. Annie Besant, South India and the Aligarh Movement

fiveW.who: Annie Besant; Kandukuri Veeresalingam; Sree Narayana Guru; Syed Ahmad Khan
fiveW.when: Late 19th – early 20th century; MAO College 1877; Home Rule 1916
fiveW.what: Theosophy, southern reform, and modern education for Muslims
fiveW.why: Revive spiritual values; uplift women and oppressed castes; educate Muslims
fiveW.how: Schools, colleges, conferences and social campaigns

notes.content:
**Annie Besant** — President of the **Theosophical Society** in India; revival of **spiritual Hinduism**; founded the **Central Hindu School, Benares**; organised the **Home Rule Movement (1916)**.

**South India**
• **Kandukuri Veeresalingam** — women's education, **widow remarriage**.
• **Sree Narayana Guru** — denounced the **rigid caste system**; upliftment of the oppressed.

**Syed Ahmad Khan and the Aligarh Movement**
• Muslim educator, jurist, author; revived the condition of **Indian Muslims**.
• Founded the **Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental (MAO) College, Aligarh (1877)** → later **Aligarh Muslim University**.
• Organised the **All-India Muhammadan Educational Conference**.
• Believed Muslims would progress through **Western scientific learning**; modelled MAO on **Oxford and Cambridge**.

notes.subtopic: 7. Singh Sabha and Impact of the Reform Movements
notes.content:
**Singh Sabha** (Amritsar and Lahore) — Sikh reform:
• **Khalsa College, Amritsar**.
• Schools for **Gurmukhi** script and **Punjabi** literature.
• Later the **Akali Movement** — purify Sikh practices and oust the British.

**Achievements of the reform movements**
• **Emancipation of women** began.
• **Widow Remarriage Act (1856)**; **sati and female infanticide banned**.
• **Girls' education** popularised; **marriage age** raised.
• **Caste system** less rigid; **Western education** adopted.
• Reform took a **nationalist flavour** and all-India reach.

**Literature:** Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay, **Sarojini Naidu**, **Tarabai Shinde**, **Subramania Bharati** — wrote in English and **regional languages**.
**Art:** **Abanindranath Tagore, Raja Ravi Varma** — fused Indian tradition with European techniques.

questions.answer: Roy-Brahmo · Dayanand-Arya · Phule-Satyashodhak · Ranade-Prarthana · Vivekananda-RK Mission · Syed Ahmad-Aligarh

questions.question: What reforms were advocated by the Brahmo Samaj under Raja Ram Mohan Roy?
questions.answer:
• Abolition of sati and child marriage.
  • Widow remarriage.
  • Rejection of the caste system.
  • Modern education for all.
  • Equal rights for women, including the right to property.

His efforts led Bentinck to ban sati.

questions.question: Who was Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar? State his contributions.
questions.answer:
• A Bengali humanist and educationist who championed the poor.
  • Campaigned for widow remarriage → Act of 1856.
  • Opened Sanskrit study to non-Brahmanas; introduced Western philosophy at Sanskrit College.
  • Helped Bethune start a girls' school (1849) and opened more.

questions.question: What were the beliefs of Swami Vivekananda?
questions.answer:
• Unity of all religions.
  • Religious tolerance, brotherhood, peace and harmony.
  • Condemned caste, inequality, ritualism and superstition.
  • Regeneration through self-discipline and social responsibility.
  • Upliftment of women.

questions.question: (Picture) Reformer who set up a samaj for the oppressed: identify him, the samaj and its aims.
questions.answer:
• (a) Jyotirao Govindrao Phule.
  • (b) Satyashodhak Samaj (1873).
  • (c) Aims: equality and dignity for the oppressed and untouchable castes, education for women and lower castes (he and Savitribai Phule opened schools for girls), and freedom from priestly domination.

questions.question: Describe the work of the Arya Samaj.
questions.answer:
• Founded by Dayanand Saraswati in 1875.
  • Opposed child marriage, idol worship and the caste system.
  • Opened Vedic study to all castes.
  • Its followers set up DAV schools blending Indian learning and Western science.

questions.question: Name the south Indian reformer who denounced the caste system. Who else worked in the south?
questions.answer: Sree Narayana Guru denounced the rigid caste system and worked for the oppressed. Kandukuri Veeresalingam worked for women's education and widow remarriage.

questions.question: When and where was the MAO College founded? What was the Aligarh Movement?
questions.answer:
• Founded by Syed Ahmad Khan at Aligarh in 1877; later became Aligarh Muslim University.
  • The Aligarh Movement promoted Western scientific education among Muslims to improve their condition; he also organised the All-India Muhammadan Educational Conference.

questions.question: Write a short note on the Singh Sabha.
questions.answer: A 19th-century Sikh reform movement set up in Amritsar and Lahore. It founded Khalsa College, Amritsar, opened schools promoting Gurmukhi and Punjabi literature, and later inspired the Akali Movement to purify Sikh practices and oust the British.

questions.question: Mention issues common to all the reform movements. What did they achieve?
questions.answer:
• Common issues: status of women (sati, child marriage, widows, education), caste rigidity, superstition and ritualism, and the need for modern education.
  • Achievements: sati and female infanticide banned; Widow Remarriage Act 1856; girls' education spread; marriage age raised; caste became less rigid; Western education adopted.

questions.question: Did the reform movements contribute to the rise of nationalism? Give reasons.
questions.answer:
Yes.

  • They created pride in India's past and self-confidence.
  • They spread rational and liberal ideas of liberty and equality.
  • They weakened caste and religious divisions, helping unity.
  • Reformers from many regions linked with the all-India national movement; e.g. Annie Besant's Home Rule Movement, the Akali Movement against the British.

questions.question: Explain the impact of the reform movements on literature and regional languages.
questions.answer:
• Educated Indians expressed ideas in newspapers, magazines and books — poems, stories, essays.
  • They wrote in English and regional languages — this enriched regional languages.
  • Famous writers: Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay, Sarojini Naidu, Tarabai Shinde, Subramania Bharati.
